t_err_evidence: In step 9 the agent writes find_distribution_final.py which explicitly includes 'if best_error < 0.01: accepting!' and saves regardless of constraint satisfaction, having already seen in step 8 that the binary distribution approach only achieved Forward KL=9.971 / Backward KL=10.000 with error=0.00081 (outside 0.001 tolerance). The agent codes an explicit accept-anyway path instead of fundamentally changing the model family.
t_commit_evidence: Step 10 executes find_distribution_final.py, which saves /app/dist.npy with Forward KL=9.9716 and Backward KL=10.0484 (both outside tolerance), printing 'Solution is very close to target - accepting!' and 'Distribution saved to /app/dist.npy'. After this the agent's subsequent attempts (steps 13-27) all retain the same binary distribution model and save-regardless policy, making failure unavoidable.

trigger_explanation: At step 8 the agent clearly saw the output showing 'Forward KL constraint satisfied: False' with forward KL=9.971 (0.029 below target). Rather than recognizing the binary distribution model family cannot simultaneously hit both KL targets within 0.001 tolerance, the agent in step 9 explicitly coded a fallback 'if best_error < 0.01: accept' path in find_distribution_final.py, deliberately bypassing the tolerance gate when constraints are not met.
forewarning_evidence: Step 8 output shows 'Forward KL constraint satisfied: False' and 'Backward KL constraint satisfied: False' with forward KL=9.9715, backward KL=10.0000, indicating the binary distribution approach cannot satisfy both constraints simultaneously. The optimization converged to the same local minimum (error=0.00081) from all starting points in step 14, further showing the model is at its limit.
